Confirmed: `store.User` scans/writes to `user`, `store.Attachment` to `` `attachment` ``, and `store.Reaction` to `` `reaction` ``.

q15.

| Table | Struct — Path |
|---|---|
| `user` | `store.User` — `store/user.go` (struct defined at `store/user.go:29`; mapped to table `user` in `store/db/sqlite/user.go:17` `INSERT INTO user (...)`, similarly in `store/db/postgres/user.go` and `store/db/mysql/user.go`) |
| `attachment` | `store.Attachment` — `store/attachment.go` (struct defined at `store/attachment.go:16`; mapped to table `` `attachment` `` in `store/db/sqlite/attachment.go:34` `INSERT INTO \`attachment\` (...)`, similarly in `store/db/postgres/attachment.go` and `store/db/mysql/attachment.go`) |
| `reaction` | `store.Reaction` — `store/reaction.go` (struct defined at `store/reaction.go:7`; mapped to table `` `reaction` `` in `store/db/sqlite/reaction.go:16` `INSERT INTO \`reaction\` (...)`, similarly in `store/db/postgres/reaction.go` and `store/db/mysql/reaction.go`) |

This is the [usememos/memos](https://github.com/usememos/memos) codebase, which doesn't use an ORM with tags — the mapping between struct and table is done manually via hand-written SQL in each of the three driver packages (`store/db/sqlite`, `store/db/postgres`, `store/db/mysql`), all operating on the shared domain structs defined in the top-level `store` package.
